slides.title:
Two brothers.
One shoe company.
Then *a feud* for life.
slides.sub:
How one family feud gave us
adidas AND Puma 👇

slides.title:
Adi and Rudolf Dassler
start making shoes in
*their mother's laundry room*.
slides.sub:
Herzogenaurach, Bavaria. Adi makes
the shoes, Rudi sells them
(History.com, Mental Floss).

slides.title:
Berlin Olympics. Jesse Owens
wins *4 gold medals*
in Dassler shoes.
slides.sub:
The brothers offered him a pair
before the Games (Mental Floss).

slides.title:
After the war, the feud
explodes. *The company
splits in two*.
slides.sub:
Rudi founds Puma (1948). Adi founds
adidas (1949), on the other side
of the river (History.com).

slides.title:
A small town *picks a side*.
Bakers, schools, even
gravestone cutters.
slides.sub:
"Because it is a small town, you kind
of chose sides" (Nick Smith, author
of Kicks, on History.com).

slides.title: We didn't even mention the name of *Adidas* actually at home.
slides.author:
Michael Dassler, Rudi's grandson
(BBC, via History.com)

slides.title:
adidas pushes *screw-in
studs*. West Germany
wins the World Cup.
slides.sub:
The "Miracle of Bern". A product
detail that made history (History.com).

slides.title:
Rudi dies. Adi follows in
1978. Buried on *opposite
sides* of the cemetery.
slides.sub:
They never made peace. Staff only
played a friendly match together
in 2009 (History.com, Mental Floss).

slides.title:
adidas revenue in 2025,
a *record*. Puma is still
its rival next door.

Great product
*+ great selling*.
slides.sub:
Adi made the shoes. Rudi sold them.
Your store needs both sides.

✅ A product page that shows the details
✅ Real photos, real reviews
✅ Put it on the right feet (creators)
✅ A clear reason to buy from you
